aic.title: Global Campus AI Algorithm Elite Competition
aic.description: The 2026 Algorithm Challenge problems and the organizer’s six track archives.

tasks.title: InstRead
tasks.description: Predict how long unseen readers look at individual words in Romanian texts.
tasks.objective: Estimate total reading time in milliseconds for each requested item. A word can be skipped entirely. Training observations include the reader and the word’s position within a text.
tasks.deliverable: A CSV with subtaskID, datapointID, and answer. Use subtaskID 1 and keep the IDs and row coverage from the organizer’s sample.
tasks.timing: Original session: 23 hours for one task. Suggested hub drill: 120 minutes after setup.
rules: Use the competition files supplied by Nitro. Review the WAICC V rules before using outside resources.
For a blind practice attempt, separate validation readers from training readers and reserve the test data for inference.
tasks.accessNote: Nitro lists Train Data, Test Data, and Sample Output under Files. Sign in for the organizer’s submission form. File and scoring access can depend on your account.

files.name: Train Data
files.description: Word-level observations with text context, word and reader identifiers, and total reading time.

files.name: Test Data
files.description: Items to predict for readers outside the training group.

files.name: Sample Output
files.description: Use this to match the three CSV columns and requested IDs.

setup: Open Nitro and obtain the three files listed under Files.
Load the CSVs in Python. Confirm the target is in milliseconds and identify the reader column.
Set aside labeled rows for whole readers. Confirm you can export an answer for every sample ID before starting the clock.
tasks.grading: The organizer’s formula is 50 × (max(0, R²) + |Pearson r|). Undefined Pearson correlation contributes zero. The statement says leaderboard scores below the baseline of 36 show as zero.
tasks.rehearsal: Use the published formula on a labeled holdout of readers and keep its score separate from Nitro’s. Save the split, elapsed time, score and export.

localTool.label: Download local scorer
localTool.description: Both files use the three output columns. This returns the raw score on your holdout.

tasks.title: PolERo
tasks.description: Classify response clarity and finer evasion strategies in Romanian interviews.
tasks.objective: Given a question and its response, predict a three-way clarity label and a nine-way evasion strategy. Each fine label belongs to exactly one clarity class. Interview context is identified in the supplied metadata.
tasks.deliverable: One CSV with subtaskID, datapointID, and answer. The contest expects 592 prediction rows: 296 for clarity (1) and 296 for evasion (2). Use the organizer’s exact label strings.
tasks.timing: Original session: 23 hours for teams of three. Suggested hub drill: 150 minutes after setup.
rules: WAICC VI allowed free public compute and pretrained models within those resources. For an offline rehearsal, stage everything you plan to use before starting.
The official split is at the turn level. Entire-interview holdouts provide a stricter local check for performance on unseen interviews.
tasks.accessNote: Nitro lists Train Data, Test Data and Sample Output. Getting files or submitting may require account access. Post-event judge access was not verified.

files.name: train_data.csv
files.description: 3,278 labeled question and response pairs, with context, transcript metadata and both labels.

files.name: test_data.csv
files.description: 296 unlabeled pairs with matching metadata.

files.name: sample_output.csv
files.description: Exact output structure for both subtasks.

setup: Open the Nitro statement and obtain its files. Keep the paper for optional reading after a blind attempt.
Check the nested label mapping and reserve whole interview URLs for local validation.
Verify that your export contains one prediction per ID per subtask.
tasks.grading: Nitro scores submitted labels against held-out answers. The public statement specifies the points per subtask without giving a complete scoring formula.
tasks.rehearsal: For local practice, report macro F1 for each subtask and check that the two labels are consistent. Treat these as local diagnostics.

tasks.title: Uneasy Alliances
tasks.description: Write a bot that coordinates a colony of simulated rats against another team.
tasks.objective: Control units in the official simulator. Collect resources, protect your king, and decide when cooperation with the opposing colony pays off. Each unit has a per-turn computation budget.
tasks.deliverable: A bot in the organizer’s scaffold, plus replays or match results against a fixed set of opponents and maps.
tasks.timing: Original tournament: multiple rounds across the season. Suggested hub drill: 120 minutes after the simulator works.
rules: Use the official match engine and supported bot APIs. Python and Java are supported, with a restricted Python library list.
Fix the maps and opponents before comparing versions. Swap sides on each map.
tasks.accessNote: Public scaffold, examples, rules and simulator. Download the engine and run a full match before timing. This task uses a local simulator.

files.name: Battlecode 2026 scaffold
files.description: Example bot, runner and submission packaging. Use Python 3.12 for the Python runner.

files.name: 2026 game specification
files.description: Game rules, units, scoring and limits.

files.name: Maps and replays
files.description: The engine runs match maps and emits replays you can inspect.

setup: Download the scaffold and read its 2026 Python documentation or Java quick start.
Run the supplied example in a match. Check that a replay is produced before changing the bot.
Keep one copy of the example bot to benchmark your submission on multiple maps.
tasks.metric: Match wins using the official simulator
tasks.grading: The simulator decides each match from the game rules. Tournament advancement uses matches against other bots. Local results depend on your map and opponent selection.
tasks.rehearsal: Save a win rate over fixed maps, opponents and swapped sides. Keep at least one replay with a loss and one with a win.

tasks.title: Industrial Quality Control
tasks.description: Identify known manufacturing defects and flag a kind of anomaly absent from training.
tasks.objective: Classify production-line images into good parts or known defects, or flag a previously unseen image as drift. Training classes are highly imbalanced, and test images include examples outside the training classes.
tasks.deliverable: Predicted labels in the challenge’s sample submission format. Reserve the final output for the Challenge Data submission page.
tasks.timing: Original challenge uses a season leaderboard. Suggested hub drill: 150 minutes after data access and setup.
rules: Open the challenge through your own Challenge Data account and follow the dataset terms.
Confirm the expected labels and the cost matrix before picking a decision threshold.
tasks.accessNote: The English statement and benchmark description are public. Downloading data and submitting require sign-in and registration for this challenge.

files.name: Training data
files.description: 8,278 images across six classes, including good parts and five defect types.

files.name: Test data
files.description: 1,055 images across seven classes, including the test-only drift class.

files.name: Cost matrix and starter reference
files.description: The challenge page shows the weighting and describes a classification plus anomaly detection benchmark.

setup: Sign in and enroll in the challenge. Download the data and submission example from Files.
Verify image names, label IDs and the image metadata in one small batch.
Set aside a reproducible development split and decide how to test rejection of unfamiliar examples.

resources.label: Sign in and get challenge files

tasks.grading: The organizer applies a cost matrix to predictions. Missing an anomaly is penalized more heavily. Compare your score with the published benchmark on Challenge Data.
tasks.rehearsal: Alongside the main score, report per-class errors and inspect which examples your model rejects.

tasks.title: EEG Cross-Task Transfer
tasks.description: Use EEG to predict reaction times and test transfer across people and tasks.
tasks.objective: Predict a participant’s response time during a visual contrast task from EEG. Explore whether learning from other recordings helps on held-out participants.
tasks.deliverable: A working prediction pipeline. Use the organizer’s submission template for the competition-style interface and save local metrics and model artifacts.
tasks.timing: Original competition had multiple stages. Suggested hub drill: 180 minutes after the starter and a mini release work.
rules: Use the competition’s downsampled releases to match the starter. Keep each participant wholly on one side of your development split.
Compare transfer and no-transfer runs using the same split and preprocessing. Save participant IDs and settings for reproducibility.
tasks.accessNote: The organizer publishes a starter, scorer, and mini data releases. Install the environment and check at least one recording before starting a timed attempt.

files.name: challenge_1.ipynb
files.description: Organizer’s notebook for loading recordings, training and evaluation.

files.name: 100 Hz mini BDF release
files.description: The small published releases have 20 participants each. Start here before downloading the full collection.

files.name: local_scoring.py and submission.py
files.description: Use the provided inference interface and local evaluation script with labeled practice data.

setup: Open the starter kit and install its dependencies into a separate Python environment.
Get a mini BDF release from the organizer’s data guide. Check the download contains the tasks you intend to use.
Run the starter against a participant-disjoint split and confirm the scorer can read your outputs.
tasks.grading: The official challenge executed submitted models on held-out people. The organizer’s local script reports prediction error and R² against labels you supply. Use the local script for practice, and report the metric and split together.
tasks.rehearsal: Start with a response-time baseline. Improve it on held-out people and document whether differences between participants or between tasks explain the results.

tasks.timing: Multi-stage organizer event. Check the required files before scheduling a practice attempt.
tasks.title: Multimodal Visual Grounding
tasks.description: Use visible, infrared and depth images to locate an object described in English.
tasks.objective: Find the specific object named by a natural-language query in a scene. Use complementary image modalities to handle low light, occlusion and visually similar objects.
tasks.deliverable: A ZIP containing the supplied query JSON with each normalized bbox filled as [x1, y1, x2, y2] for the visible image. Keep all other fields unchanged.
rules: Use the official phase test sets only for inference. The statement permits public external training data with attribution.
The organizer requires model-generated predictions and disallows commercial closed online inference APIs for the task.
tasks.accessNote: Chinese official statement. Official test data are competition-only. A public starter and a practice judge were not verified.

files.name: Visible, infrared, and depth images
files.description: Aligned inputs supplied by competition phase.

files.name: Query JSON
files.description: English descriptions and paths. Fill one box per query in the organizer’s template.

setup: Open the official statement and check the phase-specific access rules.
With authorized files, confirm image alignment and visualize a known box in the visible frame.
Check export coordinates and JSON shape before running the evaluation.
tasks.grading: Score the fraction of queries whose predicted box has intersection over union of at least 0.5 with its reference. The organizer grades submitted JSON on phase test sets.
tasks.rehearsal: With a labeled development split, compare scores by lighting and occlusion. Keep any unofficial result separate from the organizer’s score.

tasks.timing: Multi-stage organizer event. Check the required files before scheduling a practice attempt.
tasks.title: Urban Multimodal Object Detection
tasks.description: Detect multiple objects by combining RGB, infrared and depth imagery.
tasks.objective: For each synchronized image group, find each object and assign its class and confidence. Combine the sensors so detections remain useful when one view is poor.
tasks.deliverable: A ZIP of prediction TXT files, one per image group, with class, normalized box coordinates and confidence in the organizer’s specified order.
rules: Follow the current phase’s data and model restrictions on the official page. Model outputs must be reproducible.
Use the official file naming, dimensions and range requirements for normalization.
tasks.accessNote: Chinese official statement. Organizer distributes the phase files and holds the test labels. Public full-data access was not verified.

files.name: RGB, depth, and infrared image groups
files.description: The datasets include aligned views and organizer labels for development.

files.name: Per-image TXT predictions
files.description: The original page gives the exact box and confidence format.

setup: Read the output convention and permitted data rules on the official page.
With authorized data, verify matching scene IDs and inspect one labeled triplet.
Check coordinate conversion and batch export before trying a stronger detector.
tasks.metric: mAP at IoU 0.50 to 0.95, higher is better
tasks.grading: The organizer averages detection precision across classes and ten IoU thresholds. Match confidence and box quality both matter.
tasks.rehearsal: Hold out entire scenes where possible and record both the aggregate score and performance in difficult lighting.

tasks.timing: Multi-stage organizer event. Check the required files before scheduling a practice attempt.
tasks.title: Aerial Image Segmentation
tasks.description: Predict pixel labels for low-altitude aerial imagery under substantial changes in class balance.
tasks.objective: Assign land-cover or object classes such as farmland, water, roads, forest and buildings to each pixel. Test sets include scenes with different class proportions.
tasks.deliverable: One 1024 × 1024 single-channel PNG per image, using the prescribed class IDs and original names. ZIP the masks. Later phases also require reproducible materials.
rules: Submit one model. Publicly available research weights are permitted under the task rules. Follow the official training-data restriction.
Preserve image size and class IDs. Ignore-class pixels are excluded from scoring.
tasks.accessNote: Chinese official statement. The organizer links a public format example on ModelScope. Registration was required for the full contest data.

files.name: Public format example
files.description: Use it to inspect the image and mask encoding.

files.name: Organizer data
files.description: The statement lists 6,996 training images and three test releases. Full files are provided by phase.

setup: Open the public example and check that pixels are single-channel class IDs.
With authorized labels, put different scenes in training and validation sets.
Try exporting one properly sized mask before generating a submission ZIP.
tasks.metric: Mean intersection over union, higher is better
tasks.grading: For each scored class, measure overlap between predicted pixels and ground truth, divide by their union, and average over scored classes. Follow the organizer’s treatment of ignore pixels.
tasks.rehearsal: Use the public sample for format checks. Calculate scores only on authorized labeled data and report per-class IoU alongside the mean.

tasks.timing: Multi-stage organizer event. Check the required files before scheduling a practice attempt.
tasks.title: Fine-Grained Recognition with Noisy Labels
tasks.description: Adapt a fixed vision backbone to recognize many fine-grained natural categories from imperfect labels.
tasks.objective: Train a robust classifier for closely related plant and animal categories. Training labels include errors. Later stages introduce long-tail distributions and change the class population.
tasks.deliverable: ZIP the requested predictions CSV with filename and four-digit class ID. Later phases require training, inference and environment materials sufficient for reproduction.
rules: The official backbone is CLIP ViT-B/32. Submit one model or inference pipeline. The official task disallows ensembles and outside data.
Document training and any automatic treatment of noisy labels so the organizer can reproduce it.
tasks.accessNote: Chinese official statement. Organizer data are licensed for competition use only. A public starter and practice judge were not verified.

files.name: First phase
files.description: 103,218 training images across 500 categories and 24,967 test images. Later phases use different official files.

files.name: CSV submission format
files.description: The original statement shows the exact class ID and filename format.

setup: Confirm you have permission to access and use the phase data.
Plan a development split and a reproducible preprocessing run. Test the prescribed backbone on a small batch.
Check that every test image maps to exactly one output class.
tasks.grading: The organizer checks the single predicted class per image. Stage scores and the final technical defense are governed by the official rules.
tasks.rehearsal: On authorized development data, report the overall accuracy and errors by class frequency.

tasks.timing: Multi-stage organizer event. Check the required files before scheduling a practice attempt.
tasks.title: Virtual Staining for Microscopy
tasks.description: Generate a target stain image from a paired fluorescence image.
tasks.objective: Learn a mapping from DAPI microscopy images to the target assigned for the competition phase. Preserve tissue structure and alignment in the generated image.
tasks.deliverable: Place generated images under the organizer’s results folder structure, with names matched to input images. Later rounds require reproducible code, models and a report.
rules: Use the phase’s assigned stain and official data rules. The competition prohibits commercial closed generation APIs and manual correction of test outputs.
Follow the organizer’s requirements for multi-output experiments and final assessment.
tasks.accessNote: Chinese official statement. Organizer supplies paired phase-specific images. Public full-data access and score normalization code were not verified.

files.name: Paired microscopy images
files.description: DAPI input images paired with phase-specific target marker images for supervised development.

files.name: Phase test images
files.description: Input-only samples for inference. The organizer holds reference target images.

setup: Open the official rules and confirm the target marker for your phase.
With authorized pairs, check alignment, resolution and input/output file names.
Test image export and keep labeled pairs for local metric comparisons.
tasks.grading: The organizer combines structure similarity with normalized reconstruction fidelity. Later rounds use multiple test sets and the final includes a defense.
tasks.rehearsal: If you have labeled practice pairs, report SSIM and raw PSNR separately. Use the organizer’s normalization only when available.
